title: PROFILE-RELIABILITY: is the ANCHOR-level capability profile reliable, and at what cell size does reliability arrive? (zero calls)
question: The same instrument as PROFILE-TREE-ROBUST (5) at three granularities: disjoint half-splits of each cell's questions, profiles built on each half, correlated model-demeaned, Spearman-Brown to full length, averaged over 40 independent halvings, plus a cell-size sweep with the cell definition held fixed; registered: the anchor profile is publishable as a measured per-cell capability claim only if Spearman-Brown reliability >= 0.70; predicted anchor 0.35-0.60, key above 0.90, crossing at 250-400 q/cell.

plain_description.what: Measures how reproducible a model's capability profile across cells is (split-half reliability) at leaf level and at anchor/domain level, and how many questions per cell reliability needs. No calls.
plain_description.why: It decides whether per-cell capability claims from the judge can be published as measured quantities.
plain_description.information: Reliability of at least 0.70 would allow per-cell claims. Result: done. The anchor profile misses the bar (0.67 vs 0.70; leaves 0.26), so per-anchor judge profiles may not be published as measurements. About 210 questions per cell are needed, and anchors average 201. The answer-key profile is far more reliable. A later ruling classes the judge parts as history; the answer-key parts are not affected.
